summary: Masumi describes identity verification for the GWI audience-insight agent on Sokosumi. This is a potential commercial audience-data integration; public data access and a MEW partnership are not established.
Masumi announces MCP access to Sokosumi services. Repository and authentication compatibility require separate testing before MEW can dispatch jobs.
Masumi describes monetizing n8n workflows and their payment and job lifecycle. MEW should retain its own durable operation identity and reconcile uncertain outcomes.

Masumi argues that agent purchases need traceable authorization and dispute handling. Treat this as publisher analysis; legal conclusions and cited market statistics are not independently validated here. MEW should test dispute evidence export and separate delivery acceptance from settlement.

Masumi discusses HTTP-to-chain settlement races, replay and paid-response caching. This is a threat-model lead rather than independently reproduced security research. MEW still needs authenticated delivery receipts and tests against any actual payment worker before production.
